ai.description: *Hylarana garoensis* is a small frog with a brown dorsum and white belly. It features a distinct dark lateral band from the snout to the flank and possesses a pointed snout with long, slender limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hylarana garoensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dorsolateral fold that extends from behind the eye to the groin, unlike many similar species.
ai.habitat: *Hylarana garoensis* inhabits moist, evergreen tropical forests in the Garo Hills, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 500 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Garo Hills frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the damp, rocky stream banks of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana garoensis* is an oviparous breeder that lays small clutches of eggs in forest streams during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hylarana garoensis* is endemic to the Garo Hills of Meghalaya in Northeast India, typically inhabiting streams at elevations between 500 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Garo Hills Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched, pulsed notes, typically heard calling from vegetation near streams in its humid forest habitat.
